newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan court refuses "frivolous" Bhutto petition.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan court refuses "frivolous" Bhutto petition.

text.p: Pakistan's Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to accept ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's petition against her sacking, saying it contained "objectionable and scandalous portions", her lawyer and court officials said.
A court official declined to specify which parts of the petition were at issue but said the document could be re-filed with modifications.

Bhutto's lawyer, Aitzaz Ahsan, said he was surprised by the court action on the petition, which he filed last Wednesday to challenge her dismissal by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
The court rebuff came just as police arrested Bhutto's political secretary Naheed Khan on unspecified charges in the latest of a series of arrests since her sacking.
The 42-page petition had contained blistering criticism of Leghari for dismissing his former political patron and dissolving the National Assembly (lower house of parliament).
"I have also heard (about the return of the petition)," Ahsan told Reuters by telephone from his office in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore.
"The specific objection of the office of the Supreme Court has not been brought to my notice as yet," he said. "I am no doubt surprised."
Asked if he would remove the objectionable portions and file the petition again, Ahsan said he would go to the court in Islamabad on Wednesday to see what to do next.
State television said Bhutto's petition had been returned on the grounds that the language used in some portions was "improper and scandalous".

It said the court registrar had returned the petition with remarks that it had been drafted "in an argumentative manner" in contravention of a court rule, contained "frivolous, unnecessary and scandalous matter" and that it had needed modifications.
The petitioner can also appeal against the refusal of the petition before the court within 14 days, state television quoted the registrar as saying.
Ahsan said the petition had been drafted with "due deference and utmost respect and humility" keeping in view the petitions and judgements in two similar dismissals that were not upheld by courts.

Bhutto's was the fourth government to be overturned by a president in less than nine years by the use of controversial powers inserted in Pakistan's constitution by the late military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq.

The Supreme Court had upheld none of the previous dismissals and reinstated a government led by former prime minister Nawaz Sharif in 1993 a few weeks after then president Ghulam Ishaq Khan had dismissed it.

Naheed was arrested by officers from the Federal Investigation Agency police at Islamabad airport as she arrived with Bhutto from the southern city of Karachi, a spokesman for Bhutto said. It was not clear where she was headed.
There was no police comment on the arrest.

Bhutto's spokesman, Shah Mahmoud Qureshi, said Naheed had been detained under a Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, the same law authorities have used to detain Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari since November 5, but he did not know how long she would be held.
Other people already arrested include Nawaz Khokhar, the former science and technology minister, intelligence bureau chief Masood Sharif and several other government officials.
